status: MITIGATED — local depth guard verified; upstream advisory remains scanner-visible; release gate blocked

advisory.issue: Deeply nested brace patterns can trigger stack exhaustion in recursive AST walkers.

dependencyPath.development: fast-glob dependency chain; exercised by the depth-guard regression test

mitigation.coverage: Depth guards protect the recursive parse/expand paths while retaining ordinary brace expansion.

runtimeExposureAssessment.productionUse: The Clerk proxy is enabled only in production when CLERK_SECRET_KEY is configured. Its path rewrite is a literal route-prefix replacement; it does not configure a brace glob/pathFilter or accept a user-provided brace pattern.
runtimeExposureAssessment.assessment: The inspected middleware does not appear to route untrusted request data into braces pattern parsing. The local guard tests exercise the actual transitive production and development dependency chains. This is a scoped reachability assessment, not a claim that the dependency is fixed or that every package call site is harmless.

releaseImplication: The local depth guard and six regression checks mitigate the known recursion paths, and the production proxy configuration does not route untrusted data into brace-pattern parsing. The dependency audit still reports a High advisory against braces@3.0.3; do not suppress the finding or present the scanners as clean. Keep the release decision blocked until a fixed upstream release removes the finding or an authorized security exception is recorded. This remains a security blocker even though the 70-article byline and draft-date gates are resolved.
